content: Emtriva is the brand name for emtricitabine, a synthetic nucleoside analog that exhibits activity against the reverse transcriptase enzyme of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1). The chemical name of emtricitabine is 5-fluoro-1-(2R,5S)-cytosine. Structurally, emtricitabine is the enantiomer of a thio analog of cytidine, distinguished from other cytidine analogs by the presence of a fluorine atom at the 5-position. Emtricitabine appears as a white to off-white powder and has a solubility of approximately 112 mg/mL in water at 25°C. Emtriva is available in two formulations: capsules and an oral solution. The Emtriva capsules are intended for oral administration. Each capsule contains 200 mg of emtricitabine as the active ingredient, along with the following inactive ingredients: crospovidone, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, povidone, titanium dioxide, gelatin, and FD&C Blue No. 2. The Emtriva oral solution is also designed for oral administration. Each milliliter (1 mL) of the solution contains 10 mg of emtricitabine in an aqueous solution. The inactive ingredients in the oral solution include cotton candy flavor, FD&C Yellow No. 6, edetate disodium, methylparaben and propylparaben (used as preservatives), sodium phosphate (monobasic), propylene glycol, water, and xylitol (used as a sweetener). Sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid may be used to adjust the pH of the solution.
